title: Inside the Loop: A Mechanistic Study of Looped Transformers on Permutation Traversal
abstract: arXiv:2610.24135v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Solving algorithmic tasks with many sequential steps typically requires scaling up transformer depth or chain-of-thought length, incurring unfavorable parameter and inference-compute costs, respectively. Looped transformers, which reuse one block of layers across many iterations, are poised to address this, since they scale effective depth without adding parameters or tokens. Yet, it remains unclear what each iteration is actually computing, or whether the loop merely simulates a deeper untied stack. Here, we study directed permutation traversal, in which a model follows H hops from a starting node and reports the node it reaches, so every intermediate hop has a known ground truth. We find that a minimum effective depth is necessary to solve the task, beyond which the degree of weight tying becomes the determining factor. For instance, a looped transformer with a four-layer block iterated eight times solves the task in every se

translated_title: 循环内部：循环变换器在排列遍历上的机制研究
translated_abstract: 解决具有大量顺序步骤的算法任务通常需要增加变换器的深度或思维链的长度，这分别会带来不利的参数成本和推理计算成本。循环变换器在多次迭代中重复使用同一个层块，有望解决这一问题，因为它可以在不增加参数或标记的情况下扩展有效深度。然而，目前尚不清楚每次迭代实际在计算什么，或者循环是否仅仅是在模拟一个更深的不绑定权重堆栈。在本文中，我们研究了有向排列遍历任务，其中模型从起始节点出发跟随H跳并报告最终到达的节点，因此每个中间跳都有已知的真实答案。我们发现，解决该任务需要一个最小有效深度，超过此深度后，权重绑定的程度成为决定性因素。例如，一个由四层块迭代八次构成的循环变换器在每个设（原文截断）
tldr: 研究发现循环变换器解决有向排列遍历任务需要最小有效深度，超过该深度后权重绑定的程度成为决定性能的关键因素。
en_tdlr: This mechanistic study shows that looped transformers require a minimum effective depth to solve directed permutation traversal, beyond which the degree of weight tying becomes the determining factor.
